**Summary of analysis:**

The test image shows a tomato stem at the soil line with:
- White/bleached tissue at the crown area
- Small dark round sclerotia scattered on the white stem tissue
- White mycelial growth
- Healthy green tissue above the infected zone

Comparing all 8 reference classes:
- **Southern_Blight** is the best match: white mycelium at soil line with small mustard-seed-sized sclerotia (Sclerotium rolfsii). The reference image (5411390/5411388) shows nearly identical white mycelium with small sclerotia at the stem base on black plastic mulch - identical field conditions.
- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot** was close but its sclerotia are much larger (0.5-1 cm, irregular) vs. the small round dots in the test image.
- All other candidates (Alternaria, Phytophthora, Southern Bacterial Wilt, Gray Mold, Bacterial Wilt, Rhizopus) showed fundamentally different symptom patterns.
